Cyber AI Insights
White Paper
State of AI Cybersecurity 2025
Darktrace recently surveyed over 1,500 security leaders and practitioners across a multiple countries and industries, to establish their attitudes and priorities when it comes to the impact of AI on cybersecurity
Download the white paper
Evolving threats, static defenses
As cyber-criminals begin to harness offensive AI to craft more sophisticated and targeted attacks at scale, defenders face new challenges:
Multi-stage phishing attacks that leverage trusted cloud services or QR codes to deliver payloads
Novel and ever-evolving ransomware strains that evade Threat Intelligence, signature-based and rules-based approaches
Attacks that target organizations through cloud misconfigurations or zero-day vulnerabilities
Not all AI is created equal
Most AI cybersecurity solutions rely on transferring data out of the business and into large cloud-hosted databases, where attack patterns are identified, so threats can be stopped when they reoccur.
Novel is the new normal
Attackers are now using AI-driven polymorphic malware, adversarial AI techniques, and stealthy lateral movement – meaning ‘never-before-seen’ attacks are increasingly common. This renders traditional security models ineffective, and defenders need AI that can keep pace.
Self-Learning AI
Rather than learn from previously-encountered attacks, Darktrace combines multiple AI models to understand 'normal' for your organization and reveal unusual behavior.
Achieve real security outcomes
By threading together anomalies and surfacing critical security incidents to human teams, Darktrace AI helps drive measurable security outcomes.
